thread:
leo: Quick q 111 planning to be in Barcelona for 4 months (Jul 1 126 to Oct 1 126) while helping with a partner integration. Will this affect my WFH stipend / payroll / benefits?

maria (People Ops): @leo thanks for the heads up. A few clarifying q's: are you staying on Redwood payroll? Any client invoicing or are you being seconded to partner payroll?

leo: Staying on Redwood payroll. No local contract changes, just onsite collaboration. I'll still be full-time for Redwood.

oliver (Tax): Short version: anything >90 days in a foreign country can create local tax reporting risk and potentially social security obligations. Spain has specific non-resident rules and social security. 4 months is borderline. We'll need exact dates and whether you'll be paid for travel/expenses by the partner.

leo: Dates above. Partner covers local travel expenses only. No stipend from them.

maria (People Ops): Policy note: recurring WFH stipend is for your primary home workspace. For temporary international stays >30 days we usually suspend recurring stipend and allow an "international temporary workspace" reimbursement (coworking/hot desk/hotels) up to $X/week. We'll confirm amount once tax flags cleared.

dana (Benefits): Also flagging benefits continuity: health/medical coverage may be impacted for prolonged travel outside your home country. We'll check with our carrier whether 4 months is covered under existing plan, or if short-term international coverage needs to be purchased.

sam (Manager): Team is supportive. Leo, happy to provide a note about the work scope if Tax needs it.

oliver (Tax): Action items for @leo: 1) confirm exact travel dates and city address 2) confirm no local bank/payroll 3) submit the remote-location form: https://go.redwoodinference.com/remote-request (choose "International temporary")

leo: Form submitted and added address: Carrer de Balmes, Barcelona. No local bank, no local payroll.

oliver (Tax): Thanks. We'll run a Spain tax/social security checklist and aim to advise within 4 business days. Possible outcomes: OK to proceed as-is, we ask to shorten trip <90 days, or we need to set up short-term local filings.

maria (People Ops): For the stipend: while under review, please keep receipts for any coworking/hotel workspace. If approved, we'll reimburse via expense (instructions in the form confirmation).

hr-bot: Reminder: if you're taking company equipment abroad, mark assets in AssetTracker and file the temporary export form: https://assets.redwood/temporary-export.

dana (Benefits): I'll check insurer and follow up here. If additional travel medical is needed, we'll coordinate purchase and expense coding.

leo: Awesome, appreciate the fast replies. Would prefer reimbursements rather than losing stipend. Will hold off on booking long-term housing until cleared.

maria (People Ops): Understood 14 we'll update this thread when Tax & Benefits sign off. Marking status: "review in progress". :hourglass_flowing_sand:

oliver (Tax): Note for team: Spain has 183-day rule for residency but also local social security rules for short assignments. This will be fact-specific. If we need external counsel we'll loop them in.

maria (People Ops): Expected update by EOD Thursday (4 business days). If anything changes, we'll escalate. :white_check_mark:
